method: Independent read of all 14 scripts by a separate review agent (no edits, read-only checks: bash -n, py_compile, verify.sh), then fixes applied and re-verified.

findings.issue: Loaded the upstream checkout's .ate-dev-env.sh after env.sh, so a pre-existing checkout's PROJECT_ID could win and --delete-project would delete that project.
findings.fix: Teardown pins the target from env.sh, refuses if the upstream env names a different project, and refuses any project without the purpose=substrate-field-test label setup.sh applies.

findings.issue: Silently reused an existing project with the same ID, and re-pinned, patched and overwrote an existing substrate checkout.
findings.fix: Refuses an existing project without its label; clones into .upstream/substrate by default and refuses a checkout it did not create (marker file).

findings.issue: State-polling loops had no timeout. A stuck actor hung the test forever; in test 03 that leaves three agents calling the Anthropic API every 45 s.
findings.fix: Every wait has a deadline (120-180 s) and fails instead of hanging.

findings.issue: set -e exits skipped cleanup, leaving actors, egress policies or running agents behind.
findings.fix: trap cleanup EXIT in each test; test 03's trap suspends all agents.

findings.issue: Replaced the shared credential-provider namespace-policy ConfigMap and never restored it; left two namespaces behind.
findings.fix: Backs the ConfigMap up first and restores it (or deletes ours) on exit; removes both namespaces.

findings.issue: Any unrecognised flag fell through to a full teardown.
findings.fix: Unknown options exit 2 before doing anything.

findings.issue: Printed 'project deleted' even if the delete failed; verify counted a gcloud error as zero resources and skipped Artifact Registry.
findings.fix: Delete failure exits 1; listings that error show ERR and fail verification; Artifact Registry repositories are checked.

findings.issue: A failed rebuild left the old files in place so the lineage check still passed; on real drift it overwrote the originals.
findings.fix: A rebuild failure is a FAIL; originals are restored after comparison so verify never changes the repo.

findings.issue: A timed-out Job kept running into the next test; the first pod failure was read as Job failure despite retries.
findings.fix: Waits on the Job's Complete/Failed condition; deletes a timed-out Job.

findings.issue: Reported OK when stats.jsonl never arrived.
findings.fix: OK requires a Complete Job and a stats.jsonl on disk.

findings.issue: grep -q under pipefail could break gcloud's pipe and create a duplicate budget.
findings.fix: grep -x > /dev/null instead of -q.

findings.issue: go install may put kubectl-ate outside PATH; every test then fails.
findings.fix: Checks and prints the PATH line to add.

findings.issue: The published F5 log contained the (random, already deleted) injected test token.
findings.fix: Masked in the log; the test now masks it when printing.

findings.issue: grep -qw treated the dots in an IP as wildcards.
findings.fix: grep -Fqw.

findings.issue: An unknown group name deleted the current workloads and redeployed with empty arguments.
findings.fix: Unknown groups are skipped before anything is deleted.

findings.issue: Silently skipped the bash 3.2 patch when it no longer applied.
findings.fix: Distinguishes applied / already applied / no longer applies, and says which.

findings.issue: Python 3.9/3.10 fromisoformat rejects Go's variable-length fractional seconds.
findings.fix: Parses whole seconds with strptime and adds the fraction.

findings.issue: Crashed if the oversubscription run was missing.
findings.fix: Guarded.

findings.issue: Wrote output relative to the current directory.
findings.fix: Paths are relative to the repo; tests cd to the repo root.

findings.issue: --replace without '=' crashed (an empty OLD would corrupt files); a trailing --forbid tripped set -u.
findings.fix: Both validated with a clear error.

findings.issue: setup.sh has never been run end to end; it was assembled from steps that were each run individually during the field test.
findings.fix: Stated in the README. A clean-room run is the next validation step.
